title: Bangladesh's Shrimp Sector: Export Trends, Value Chain Linkages, and Road to Sustainable Growth
content:
ABSTRACT

Shrimp is among the most economically significant commodities in global aquaculture, representing approximately 16% by value of globally traded aquatic animal products. Bangladesh has historically been a major producer and exporter, with its industry dominated by black tiger shrimp (Penaeus monodon) and giant freshwater prawn (Macrobrachium rosenbergii). However, growing structural, environmental, and institutional challenges threaten the sector's sustainability and international competitiveness. This study presents a comprehensive sectoral assessment of Bangladesh's shrimp industry amid post-COVID market disruptions, accelerating climate-related risks, and intensifying competition from Litopenaeus vannamei-based systems in major competing nations. The analysis integrates 40 years of secondary statistics with large-scale primary survey data (n = 8924). The study examines the historical development of shrimp farming, production and export trends, supply chain and value chain structure, post-harvest losses, and sectoral challenges. Key findings reveal that total farm-system production has increased through both area expansion and improvements in average yield, although traditional shrimp farming continues to face productivity constraints relative to more intensive systems in competing countries. Bangladesh's share of the global shrimp export market has declined substantially, while post-harvest losses remain a significant and largely preventable economic burden. Additional constraints include fragmented value-chain coordination, weak traceability and quality assurance systems, and slow adoption of modern aquaculture technologies. The study also identifies the recent introduction of L. vannamei as both an opportunity and a biosecurity challenge. The findings underscore the need for coordinated interventions by the government, the private sector, and development organizations to restore Bangladesh's global competitiveness in shrimp.
